structs.name: CExecuteRebelAcceptanceCommand
structs.comment: **A command that tells the players a country has accepted its rebels' demands, and stamps its last_rebel_acceptance - and that nothing in this build ever posts.** CCommand (0x3C) and one CEventScope (0x48) at +0x3C, whose country is the accepting country and whose rebel_faction id pair names the faction. Type id 0x647. Its vftable is written only by its constructor (called once, by RegisterCommandTypes, to make the prototype) and by its Clone, and the type id 0x647 is pushed nowhere else, so a live one can only arrive through the command channel's prototype table. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section D.7.
structs.evidence: findRefs.py --vftable CExecuteRebelAcceptanceCommand: the table 0x15C4344 is written at 0x55B65F (the constructor 0x55B5F0, one caller 0x886E23 inside RegisterCommandTypes 0x885050..0x887F37) and 0x55BDEA (Clone, which asks operator new for 0x84 - read in the decompiler - and copies the scope from this+0x3C into new+0x3C with CEventScope::CopyConstruct). RTTI export: base CCommand at 0, one table at 0x15C4344, 15 slots. findRefs.py --address 0x647: only the constructor (0x55B633), GetTypeId (0x55BD30) and an unrelated LoadKey switch (0x524693, sub eax,0x647 on a token). Would be shown wrong by a code path that builds the object without either of those two writers - none was found by the vftable scan.

addresses.name: RunDailyRebelFactionPass
addresses.comment: **One rebel faction's day**, read whole on the listing (0x4B9D60 to the `ret 4` at 0x4BA4CD; **0x4BA4D0 abuts it with no padding and is a different function, the monthly pass**). RunDailyPass calls it on every faction at 0x682E78 and deletes those whose wants_removal (+0x90) it set. In order: (1) RebelFaction_ResilientRetreat (0x4BD4E0). (2) **Death test 1**: the faction's country (+0x38) owns no province (NumberOfOwnedProvinces +0xCF8 <= 0) and the type's area (+0x180) is 0 (`nation`) - wants_removal and return. (3) **Death test 2**: an independence country (+0x48 non-zero) that owns a province - wants_removal and return. (4) **The provinces**: for each id in +0x94 (0x10-byte nodes, next at +8): a province controlled by REB with an owner is kept on a local list when RebelFaction_IsFriendlyCountry(faction, owner); a province **not** controlled by REB, or unowned, is taken off +0x94 (marked at node +0xC instead while the list's guard +0xA0 is set; count +0x9C decremented). Then **each kept province is handed back to its owner**: Province_SetController(province, owner, now (CCurrentGameState +0xBDC), applyConsequences 1, rebuildAreas 0, peaceful 0). (5) **Unconditionally** DeleteAreaGroups, RebuildAreaGroups, DeleteSupplyGroups, RebuildSupplyGroups - every faction, every day. (6) **The armies** (+0x80, 0x14-byte nodes holding a unit's object id pair, next at +0xC): each whose unit no longer exists (FindPersistentByIdPair) or whose owner id (CUnit +0x128) is not units_owner's (+0x50, REB) is taken off (marked while +0x8C is set; +0x88 decremented). (7) **Death test 3**: no armies (+0x88 == 0) and no provinces (+0x9C == 0) - wants_removal and return. (8) **Movement**, for each army's unit that is not moving (+0x140 <= 0), not retreating (+0x158 clear) and not fighting (combats_count +0x11C <= 0): `idle = !RebelFaction_IsHostileProvince(faction, unit's province)`; `target = RebelFaction_ChooseMoveTarget(faction, unit)`; with no target and an idle unit, target = the faction's province (+0x34) where that is hostile; where it is not and its controller is friendly, **the unit is disbanded**: RebelFaction_RemoveArmy then CGameState::RemoveUnit(state, unit, 0, 1). With a target: CPathFind::Find(unit, its province, target) and the path is cut after the first province, walking it in order, that is in the faction's reach (area != 0, or owned by the faction's country) and whose owner or controller is not friendly - or after its first province where none is - then SetUnitPath(unit, path, clear 1). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section D.
addresses.revises: The record said the faction pass then builds a list 'what that list is for is not established', and FINDINGS-revolt.md put a Random() at 0x4BA9D4 inside it. Read to its end: the list is the provinces handed back to their owners through Province_SetController (0x4BA03D); the function ends at the ret 4 at 0x4BA4CD, and 0x4BA9D4 is in 0x4BA4D0, a separate monthly function abutting it with no int3 (trap 2). Added: the unconditional area and supply group rebuild, the army cleanup, a third death test (no armies and no provinces), and the movement and disbanding orders.

addresses.name: RebelFaction_ResilientRetreat
addresses.comment: **What `resilient` and `smart` do: a resilient faction's units break off battles they should not be in.** Nothing at all unless the type's resilient (+0x198) is set - **no type in Their Finest Hour or BlackICE is resilient**, so in both this is a no-op. Otherwise, for each of the faction's units (RebelFaction_CollectUnits) that is in a battle and in a province, once per unit (a unit already weighed in another's battle is skipped), over its battles until one acts: the rebels are taken to be the attackers, and the sides swapped when units_owner's id (+0x50) is among the defender's countries. **(a) A battle against a friendly country** (RebelFaction_IsFriendlyCountry true of any enemy country) - retreat. **(b) Otherwise, only when smart (+0x19A)**: units marching into the battle province (path end, CUnit +0x13C) from neighbouring land provinces (edge kind != 3) are added, REB-owned to ours and the rest to theirs; ourBrigades = sum of regiments_count (+0x40) of our land units (slot 15), at least 1; theirBrigades likewise; ratio = theirs/ours (thousandths); **below 750 (floorf 750.5) nothing**; else ourPower and theirPower are the sums of CUnit::GetPower (slot 27), ourPower 10 when 0 (floorf 10.5); dice d = theirDice - ourDice (side +0x50): d > 0 multiplies theirPower by (1000 + d*1000/18)/1000, d < 0 multiplies ourPower by (1000 - d*1000/4.5)/1000 (floorf 4500.5); score = theirPower/ourPower * ratio; **above 5000 (floorf 5000.5) - retreat**. **Retreat**: over the province's neighbours by edge (kind != 3), land, and RebelFaction_IsHostileProvince: score = +1000 per regiment of each REB-owned unit there and -1000 per regiment of any other, +4000 when REB controls it, -10000 when its controller is friendly; the strictly highest above -1000 (floorf -999.5) wins, first of equals. Then each of our units that is the faction's: standing in the battle province - CPathFind::Find to it, cut to one province, SetUnitPath(unit, path, 1); marching in - CUnit::CancelMovement(unit, 1) unless already retreating. `ret 4` at 0x4BE092. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section D.2.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4BD4E0..0x4BE092: resilient test `mov al,[eax+0x198]; test; je 0x4BE082` at 0x4BD4FE..0x4BD511; RebelFaction_CollectUnits at 0x4BD558; side swap on +0x50 in defender +0x54 countries at 0x4BD692..0x4BD6E2; friend test 0x4B98D0 at 0x4BD704; smart test +0x19A at 0x4BD722; ratio and floorf(0x160A614 = 750.5) at 0x4BD9E5..0x4BDA03; GetPower slot 0x6C at 0x4BDA45/0x4BDAC4; floorf(0x160A680 = 10.5) at 0x4BDAE3; d*1000*1000/18000 by 0x7482296B>>13 at 0x4BDB20..0x4BDB37 (0x4650 = 18000 on the slow path 0x4BDB4C); floorf(0x160AAE4 = 4500.5) at 0x4BDB81; floorf(0x160A9F8 = 5000.5) at 0x4BDC6B; floorf(0x160AAD0 = -999.5) at 0x4BDC96; scores +0x3E8/-0x3E8 per +0x40 at 0x4BDDF0..0x4BDE06, +0xFA0 at 0x4BDE27, -0x2710 at 0x4BDE47; SetUnitPath 0x5C9AC0 at 0x4BDF62, CancelMovement 0x5C9430 at 0x4BDF9F. Constants read with image.read. Would be shown wrong by a second reader of +0x198 that gates the same behaviour - the image-wide scan for byte reads of +0x198..+0x19B found this, CUnit::RetreatFromCombat (0x5C5E2A) and unrelated classes.

addresses.name: RebelFaction_IsFriendlyCountry
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall RebelFaction_IsFriendlyCountry(CRebelFaction* faction@EAX, char tag[4]@stack:4, int countryId@stack:8) @AL
addresses.comment: **Whether the rebels count a country as on their side**: true when the faction has no targets (+0x70); otherwise false as soon as one target is the country itself, or is a country the country is not at war with (country->diplomacy[target]->war, CDiplomacyStatus +0x20, null) unless the target or the country is REB. So **friendly = none of the faction's targets, and at war with every one of them**. 16 call sites in 6 functions: CCombatManager::CheckForCombat (twice, choosing who takes a province a rebel unit captures), RebelFaction_IsHostileProvince, RebelFaction_ChooseMoveTarget, RunDailyRebelFactionPass, RebelFaction_ResilientRetreat and RebelFaction_CollectIndependenceCandidates. `ret 8`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4B98D0..0x4B995E: `mov esi,[eax+0x70]`, result byte [ebp-1] = 1, empty list -> `mov al,1; ret 8`; GetCountry(&arg) once; per node: `cmp ecx(node id), edi(country +0xCA8); je false`; `[[country+0xE28]+id*4]+0x20` non-zero keeps; node tag R/E/B keeps; country +0xCA4 R/E/B keeps; else false; next at node +0xC. Both exits `ret 8`. findRefs --callers: 16 sites, 0x430BB4/0x430BE0 in CheckForCombat (0x430960). Would be shown wrong by a caller passing something other than a CCountryTag by value - every site pushes an id then a tag dword.

addresses.name: RebelFaction_IsHostileProvince
addresses.comment: **A province the rebels want**: false when the type's area (+0x180) is 0 (`nation`) and the province's owner is not the faction's country (+0x3C); false when both its owner and its controller are friendly (RebelFaction_IsFriendlyCountry); true otherwise. Bare `ret`. Five callers: RunDailyRebelFactionPass (twice), RebelFaction_ResilientRetreat, RebelFaction_IsIndependenceProvince and CUnit::FindRetreatProvince (rva 0x1C5D50, at VA 0x5C5FC0). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4B9970..0x4B99C1: `mov eax,[edi+0x30]; cmp [eax+0x180],0; jne`; `cmp [esi+0x330],[edi+0x3c]; je`; else `xor al,al; ret`; two calls to 0x4B98D0 with eax = edi on owner (+0x32C/+0x330) then controller (+0x334/+0x338); both true -> false, else `mov al,1; ret`. Would be shown wrong by a caller that does not load edi/esi first - all five load them (e.g. 0x4BA21C/0x4BA221).

addresses.name: RebelFaction_ChooseMoveTarget
addresses.comment: **Where a rebel unit goes: the province scoring highest on its type's movement_evaluation.** Null for a null unit. **When the type is both reinforcing (+0x199) and smart (+0x19A)**: null (stay) when UnitSumStrength / regiments_count is below 660 thousandths (floorf 660.5) - 0.66 of strength per brigade, where a full Their Finest Hour brigade is 30.000. Then **one Random() draw** seeds a CEventScope (country ---, the province set per candidate at +0x28). Only when the unit's province is in a real area (COwnerArea slot 0): the candidates are every province of that area (+0x24 list) and then of each area it touches (+0x34, COwnerAreaLink->area, in link order), each taken where it is in reach (area != 0, or owned by the faction's country +0x3C) and its owner or controller is not friendly; score = CMeanTimeToHappen::GetDays(&type->movement_evaluation (+0x44), scope), **halved (floorf 500.5 / 1000) when the candidate is not an edge-neighbour of the unit's province**; the strictly highest above 0 wins, first of equals in that walk order. `ret 8`. One caller, RunDailyRebelFactionPass (0x4BA238). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4B99D0..0x4B9D51: +0x199 and +0x19A at 0x4B99F1/0x4B99FE; floorf(0x160A654 = 660.5) at 0x4B9A0B; UnitSumStrength 0x5C3120 at 0x4B9A31 against +0x40 * 1000; Random 0xAA2F80 at 0x4B9A8F into CEventScope::CEventScope 0x9C1610 (edx = draw); area slot 0 at 0x4B9AB4; area +0x24 walk 0x4B9ABE..0x4B9BE8 and +0x34 walk 0x4B9BF1..0x4B9D42; GetDays 0x9C4B90 with eax = type+0x44 at 0x4B9B4F/0x4B9C9F; neighbour search over template +0x90..+0x94 stride 0x14 to_province +4; floorf(0x160A5E8 = 500.5) at 0x4B9BA2; `cmp eax,[ebp-4]; jle` keeps the first strict maximum; best starts 0 at 0x4B9AB1. Would be shown wrong by a GetDays result that is not the factor product - FINDINGS-revolt.md section 2 read GetDays.

addresses.name: RunMonthlyRebelFactionPass
addresses.comment: **Defection and independence, once a month**: RunMonthlyPass calls it on every faction at 0x683CF6, after its other work. 0x4BA4D0 (abutting RunDailyRebelFactionPass, no padding) to the `ret 4` at 0x4BAA14. **Without an independence country (+0x48 == 0) - defection**: for each province on +0x94 controlled by REB, with no land battle (combat slot 11 == 1) and not its owner's capital (+0xE20): date = ProvinceHistory_LatestControllerDate(province history, units_owner REB) + defect_delay (+0x194) months (AddMonths); **the first such province whose date is still ahead ends the whole pass**; otherwise target = RebelFaction_GetDefectionTarget(faction) - **which always answers ---** - so nothing happens (the code behind it, Province_Defect and the move of the province's rebel units to the target, is unreachable). **With one - independence**: the candidates are RebelFaction_CollectIndependenceCandidates; none, nothing; date = the earliest of their ProvinceHistory_LatestControllerDate (starting from CDefines end_date) + defect_delay months; still ahead, nothing; then ratio = candidates / RebelFaction_CollectIndependenceProvinces(faction, ---) (the same predicate, so 1), chance = ratio * 100000/1000 * 150/1000 (floorf 100000.5, 150.5) = **15 per cent a month**, rounded to nearest by fistp; Random() % 100 below it - RebelFaction_GrantIndependence(faction, ---). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4BA4D0..0x4BAA14: +0x48 test at 0x4BA573; REB controller at 0x4BA621..0x4BA642; combats +0x2EC slot 0x2C == 1 at 0x4BA648..0x4BA661 (CLandCombat slot 11 is `mov eax,1`, naval 2, air 3); capital +0xE20 vs +0xD0 at 0x4BA676; 0x4A0920 with eax = province+0xD8 and &faction+0x4C at 0x4BA699; AddMonths 0x4B8C90 with type+0x194 at 0x4BA6AB; `cmp [ebp-0x20] (gs+0xBDC), date; jl 0x4BAA04` (the epilogue) at 0x4BA6B6; 0x4BC800 at 0x4BA6C0 and its id test at 0x4BA6C5; independence branch 0x4BA84F..0x4BA9F7: 0x4BE3D0, GetDefines()+0xC, cmovg min, AddMonths, 0x4BE150 with ---/0, floorf(0x160A718 = 100000.5) and floorf(0x160A83C = 150.5), divsd by 1000.0 (0x160A300), fld/fistp, Random at 0x4BA9D4, `% 0x64`, 0x4BE590 at 0x4BA9F7. 0x4BC800 read whole: its loop over every country keeps nothing. Would be shown wrong by a different caller of 0x4BC800's out tag in this function - there is one call.

addresses.name: RebelFaction_GetDefectionTarget
addresses.comment: **The country rebels defect to - always none.** With the type's defection (+0x18C) 0 it writes --- / 0. Otherwise it walks every country of the database (+0x168 count, +0x16C array) comparing each tag's first two letters with R, E and keeping nothing, then writes the same --- / 0: **the choice was compiled to an empty loop**, so no rebel faction ever defects. `ret 4`. Nine callers: RunMonthlyRebelFactionPass (0x4BA6C0) and the rebel arms of CAddCoreEffect::Execute and ::GetTargetText, CRemCoreEffect::Execute and ::GetTargetText, CSecedeProvinceEffect::Execute (twice) and CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate and ::GetText - each asks it when the faction's type has defection, else uses the faction's independence country. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4BC800..0x4BC8F7: defection test at 0x4BC821/0x4BC82D, early arm writes 0x2D2D2D and 0 into [edi]/[edi+4]; the loop 0x4BC8B0..0x4BC8D7 only loads +0xCA4/+0xCA8 into registers and compares bytes, with no store and no branch out; [esp+0x10] (0x2D2D2D, set at 0x4BC85F) and [esp+0x1C] (0, 0x4BC856) are written to [edi] at 0x4BC8E1/0x4BC8E8 untouched. Both exits `ret 4`. Callers by E8 scan; their functions by image.functionStart and the record. Would be shown wrong by a store into [esp+0x10] or [esp+0x1C] inside the loop - there is none.

addresses.name: RebelFaction_CollectIndependenceCandidates

addresses.name: RebelFaction_GrantIndependence
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall RebelFaction_GrantIndependence(CRebelFaction* faction, char tag[4], int countryId) @AL
addresses.comment: **Rebels win their independence.** False unless the faction has an independence country (+0x48). Provinces = RebelFaction_CollectIndependenceProvinces(faction, tag, countryId); none - false. The distinct owners of those provinces are noted; ReleaseProvinces(provinces, independence country) (rva 0xC1430: owner changes, cores, technology, three-brigade armies, the INDEPENDANCE message); then **every unit of the faction** is taken off its armies list, leaves its battles (marked retreating where it held ground), has its leader moved from REB's active leaders to the new country's, and changes owner to the independence country (CUnit_SetOwner, CCountry::AddUnit, CUnit::RebuildAvatar, CUnit::EnterProvince, intel level refreshed). The faction's government (+0x40), where set, **becomes the new country's** (CCountry +0xDFC, directly). **Only when countryId is 0**: for each distinct former owner a new CWar is made, dated now and appended to the active wars, the new country attacker and the former owner defender, revolutionary_war (+8) set, named by CWar::GenerateName(war, 1). wants_removal (+0x90) set; true. `ret 0xC`. Two callers: RunMonthlyRebelFactionPass with --- (so with the wars) and CReleaseVassalEffect::Execute for `release_vassal = REB` with the scope's country (0x9AEC75). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4BE590..0x4BEBD6: +0x48 at 0x4BE5B3; 0x4BE150 at 0x4BE5D8; owner list 0x4BE5F6..0x4BE670; ReleaseProvinces 0x4C1430 at 0x4BE689 with +0x44/+0x48; CollectUnits at 0x4BE6A4; per unit 0x4BEEE0, IsHoldingGround 0x5C0160 and +0x158 = 1, LeaveAllCombats 0x5BFF70, CUnit_SetOwner 0x5BC460 at 0x4BE82C, AddUnit 0x4E06F0, leader list 0x5102C0, RebuildAvatar 0x5BDC70, EnterProvince 0x5BEFD0; government `mov esi,[faction+0x40]; mov [country+0xDFC],esi` at 0x4BE9AD..0x4BE9BC; `cmp [ebp+0x10],0; jne` at 0x4BE9C2; CWar::CWar 0xA4D6D0, gs +0xBDC into war+0xC, append to gs +0xC00/+0xC04/+0xC08, AddAttacker 0xA4F220, AddDefender 0xA506B0, `mov byte [edi+8],1` at 0x4BEB71, GenerateName 0xA4DB50 with push 1; +0x90 = 1 at 0x4BEB8B. Would be shown wrong by a war created when countryId is non-zero - the jne skips the whole block.

Callers pass eax = province+0xD8, and the record says the history is saved only while province +0xEC (history +0x14) is above zero, which is the count of a CList at +0xC. The backward direction is inferred from that layout, not from the add routine, which was not read.

addresses.name: Province_Defect
addresses.comment: **A province defects to another country - unreachable in this build**, its only caller being behind RebelFaction_GetDefectionTarget, which always answers ---. Where newOwner is real and owns a province: the old owner gets a casus belli on it (AddCasusBelli), CMapProvince::SetOwner(province, new, now, 1, 0) and Province_SetController(province, new, now, 1, 1, 0); then one message with COUNTRY = the new owner's name and PROV = the province's: THEYDEFECT when the player is the new owner, WEDEFECT when the player was the owner, OTHERDEFECT otherwise. `ret 8` at 0x4C10FF. The name is ours.

Would be shown wrong by a branch order that differs from the decompiler's (player == new owner tested first).

addresses.name: RebelFaction_TakeProvince
addresses.comment: **Rebels take a province - the 'siege won'.** Called by Province_SetController when REB becomes the controller of an owned province with units, for the faction of the first REB unit there not already holding it, and by SpawnFullRevoltInProvince. Builds a CEventScope with **one Random() draw** as its seed and random state, country --- and from --- (no country), rebel_faction = the faction's own id pair (+8/+0xC) and province = the province. Where the type's siege_won_trigger (+0x60, slot 6) holds: **if the province's owner is the player** (CCurrentGameState +0xC34), RebelType_GetSiegeEffectText(type, scope) and, only when that text is longer than one character, a REVOLTSIEGE message - the owner's message variables with MESSENGER from MESSAGE_HEAD_MARS ('The General Staff reports'), REBELS = the faction's name (+0x54), EFFECT = the text, PROV = the province's name, sender units_owner (REB) - REVOLTSIEGE has no message type in the base game or Their Finest Hour, so it goes out as the null type; then, **for any owner**, siege_won_effect (+0x120, slot 11) runs with that scope. Then, trigger or not, the province id is appended to the faction's provinces (+0x94, 0x10-byte node; count +0x9C). `ret 8` at 0x4BD4B6.
addresses.revises: Raised from inferred (decompiler) to confirmed on the listing, with the scope it runs in (no country; the faction's id as rebel_faction; a fresh Random() seed), the condition the message also needs (the effect's text longer than one character), and that the effect runs whoever owns the province. The second argument is a province id, and the first a CRebelFaction*.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4BCBB0..0x4BD4B6: Random 0xAA2F80 at 0x4BCC67 into scope +0x8/+0xC/+0x2C (esp+0x80/+0x84/+0xA4); --- into +0x10 and +0x18 (0x4BCC6F..0x4BCC87); faction +8/+0xC into +0x20/+0x24 (0x4BCC8E..0x4BCCBE); province id into +0x28 (0x4BCD13); `add ecx,0x60` and slot 0x18 call at 0x4BCCC5..0x4BCD20, `je 0x4BD460`; `cmp [province+0x330], [gs+0xC34]; jne 0x4BD446` at 0x4BCDAF..0x4BCDBF; 0x4BF690 at 0x4BCDD5 and `cmp [esp+0xd4],1; jle` (the string's length) at 0x4BCDE5; strings MESSAGE_HEAD_MARS, MESSENGER, REBELS (+0x54 at 0x4BCFC3), EFFECT, PROV, REVOLTSIEGE; PostMessage_CMessageHandler 0x434290 at 0x4BD3BA; siege_won_effect `mov eax,[ecx+0x120]; mov eax,[eax+0x2c]` at 0x4BD449 reached from both the message path and 0x4BCDBF; append at 0x4BD460..0x4BD49F. grep of interface/messagetypes.txt and tfh/interface/messagetypes.txt: no REVOLTSIEGE.

addresses.name: CExecuteRebelAcceptanceCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: **Slot 6.** Does nothing unless the scope's rebel_faction id pair (+0x5C/+0x60) resolves (FindPersistentById, the high or low table by type 0x1268).
